import sys


def merge_sorted(a, b):
    out = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
        if a[i] <= b[j]:
            out.append(a[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(b[j])
            j += 1
    while i < len(a):
        out.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    while j < len(b):
        out.append(b[j])
        j += 1
    return out


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    m = int(data[1 + n])
    b = list(map(int, data[2 + n:2 + n + m]))

questions.title: Quickselect the Kth Smallest
questions.description:
A metrics service answers kth-smallest queries on live percentiles without sorting everything: quickselect partitions around the last element and recurses into one side only. Values are distinct.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def quickselect_kth(values, k):

values holds DISTINCT integers. Return the k-th smallest value (1-indexed) using iterative quickselect: repeatedly Lomuto-partition (last-element pivot, <=) around a shrinking [lo, hi] window until the pivot lands on index k-1.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n distinct integers.
Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the k-th smallest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 500
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
1 <= k <= n
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def quickselect_kth(values, k):
    a = values[:]
    lo, hi = 0, len(a) - 1
    target = k - 1
    while True:
        pivot = a[hi]
        i = lo - 1
        for j in range(lo, hi):
            if a[j] <= pivot:
                i += 1
                a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
        a[i + 1], a[hi] = a[hi], a[i + 1]
        p = i + 1
        if p == target:
            return a[p]
        if p < target:
            lo = p + 1
        else:
            hi = p - 1


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    k = int(data[1 + n])
    print(quickselect_kth(values, k))


main()

questions.title: Quicksort the List
questions.description:
The final boss of the week: full quicksort by hand. Partition around the last element, recurse on both sides — no builtin sorting.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def quicksort_list(values):

Sort a copy of values ascending with recursive quicksort: write a partition(...) helper (Lomuto, last-element pivot, <=) and recurse on the two sides. Return the sorted list.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted list, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def quicksort_list(values):
    def partition(arr, lo, hi):
        pivot = arr[hi]
        i = lo - 1
        for j in range(lo, hi):
            if arr[j] <= pivot:
                i += 1
                arr[i], arr[j] = arr[j], arr[i]
        arr[i + 1], arr[hi] = arr[hi], arr[i + 1]
        return i + 1

    def quicksort(arr, lo, hi):
        if lo < hi:
            p = partition(arr, lo, hi)
            quicksort(arr, lo, p - 1)
            quicksort(arr, p + 1, hi)

    a = values[:]
    quicksort(a, 0, len(a) - 1)
    return a


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = quicksort_list(values)
    print(' '.join(map(str, result)))


main()

questions.title: Count the Inversions
questions.description:
A photo-album fixer counts how out-of-order a big sequence is. The brute-force double loop is too slow for the archive, so count inversions DURING the merges of merge sort.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def inversion_count(values):

Count pairs i < j with values[i] > values[j] using merge sort: while merging two sorted halves, every time an element of the right half goes first, it is smaller than all remaining left-half elements — add that many inversions at once. Return the total.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the number of inversions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def inversion_count(values):
    def sort_count(arr):
        if len(arr) <= 1:
            return arr[:], 0
        mid = len(arr) // 2
        left, li = sort_count(arr[:mid])
        right, ri = sort_count(arr[mid:])
        merged = []
        inv = li + ri
        i = j = 0
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right[j])
                j += 1
                inv += len(left) - i
        while i < len(left):
            merged.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        while j < len(right):
            merged.append(right[j])
            j += 1
        return merged, inv

    return sort_count(values)[1]


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    result = inversion_count(values)
    print(result)


main()

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def median_two(a, b):

a and b are sorted ascending and len(a) + len(b) is odd. Return the element at index (len(a) + len(b)) // 2 of the conceptual merge, advancing through both lists with two pointers.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the length of a.
Line 2: n integers, a ascending.
Line 3: m, the length of b.
Line 4: m integers, b ascending.

Output Format:
One line with the combined median element.

import sys


def median_two(a, b):
    need = (len(a) + len(b)) // 2
    i = j = 0
    last = 0
    while i + j <= need:
        if i < len(a) and (j >= len(b) or a[i] <= b[j]):
            last = a[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            last = b[j]
            j += 1
    return last


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    a = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    m = int(data[1 + n])
    b = list(map(int, data[2 + n:2 + n + m]))
    result = median_two(a, b)
    print(result)

    for i in range(n):
        m = i
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            if a[j][1] > a[m][1] or (a[j][1] == a[m][1] and a[j][0] < a[m][0]):
                m = j
        a[i], a[m] = a[m], a[i]
    return [p[0] for p in a]


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    pairs = []
    idx = 1
    for _ in range(n):
        pairs.append((data[idx], int(data[idx + 1])))
        idx += 2
    names = leaderboard(pairs)
    print('\n'.join(names))


main()
